forces.title: Data Center and GCC Expansion Drives Enterprise Hardware Demand
forces.description: The rapid expansion of data centers and Global Capability Centers (GCCs) in India, particularly in states like Karnataka and Telangana, is a significant tailwind. These facilities are critical consumers of enterprise IT hardware such as servers, storage, and specialized PCs. Their projected growth, aiming to triple water demand by 2030, directly indicates a commensurate increase in the procurement and deployment of sophisticated computing and storage infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Government Incentives Boost Domestic IT Hardware Manufacturing
forces.description: The Indian government's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for IT Hardware, including laptops, tablets, and servers, is a strong tailwind. This scheme has already generated Rs. 16,531 crore (US$1.87 billion) in production and attracted Rs. 856.64 crore (US$96.94 million) in investments by December 2025. Such initiatives reduce import dependence, foster local ecosystem development, and enhance the competitiveness of domestic manufacturers of enterprise devices.

forces.title: Surging AI Adoption Fuels Demand for High-Performance Computing
forces.description: The record pace of AI adoption in India and the emphasis on AI-enabled software investments represent a significant tailwind for enterprise hardware. Advanced analytics and generative AI applications require immense computational power, driving demand for high-performance servers, specialized processors (e.g., GPUs), and large-scale storage solutions. This transition positions robust and capable enterprise devices as indispensable for supporting India's AI ambitions.
forces.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

forces.title: Accelerated Growth in India's Domestic IT Hardware Market
forces.description: India's domestic IT Hardware market is undergoing a structural expansion, projected to grow from US$22.61 billion in 2026 to US$31.39 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 6.78%. This growth is driven by increasing domestic demand for enterprise PCs, servers, storage, and peripherals as businesses digitalize. The market's significant domestic share highlights a fundamental shift towards greater adoption and investment in local IT infrastructure, reducing reliance on imports.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Global IT Expenditure and Data Center Spending Soar
forces.description: Global IT expenditure, coupled with an anticipated 36.9% YoY surge in server expenditure and a 31.7% climb in data center spending (exceeding US$650 billion in 2026), signifies a major structural shift. This massive increase in global IT infrastructure investment creates a favorable environment for Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices, as these trends directly translate into heightened demand for servers, storage, and supporting enterprise hardware.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Development of Domestic Semiconductor and Component Supply Chains
forces.description: The expansion of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with an outlay of US$4.53 billion (Rs. 40,000 crore) aims to strengthen domestic supply chains for chips and components. While primarily focused on IN080306 and IG0804, this initiative acts as a significant tailwind for IN080302 by ensuring a more reliable and cost-effective supply of critical inputs for the manufacturing of enterprise IT hardware within India, reducing dependencies and potentially lowering production costs.

forces.title: Major Hyperscaler Investment in AI Hub and Data Center Infrastructure
forces.description: Google's US$15 billion investment in an AI Hub and data center in Visakhapatnam, from 2026-2030, represents a substantial upside driver. This significant capital commitment directly translates into increased demand for enterprise servers, storage, and associated hardware to power advanced AI capabilities and cloud services. Such large-scale projects by hyperscalers accelerate the deployment of cutting-edge enterprise devices.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Resource Scarcity Poses Long-Term Constraint for Data Center Expansion
forces.description: The 'Circular Economy' report highlights that water-intensive sectors like data centers face increasing pressure from resource scarcity, particularly water. As data center expansion intensifies, the mounting demand for water, energy, and raw materials could become a binding constraint. This poses a key risk to the sustained growth of data center infrastructure, potentially limiting the demand for servers, storage, and other enterprise hardware in the long term, especially in water-stressed regions.
forces.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

forces.title: Extensive Digital Infrastructure Investment Underpins Hardware Demand
forces.description: India's substantial investment in digital infrastructure, with approximately US$70 billion already in progress and an additional US$90 billion announced, creates a robust foundation for the Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices sector. This commitment, alongside a proposed tax holiday for cloud services via data centers, drives broad-based demand for the underlying enterprise hardware necessary to build and maintain this expansive digital ecosystem, including servers, storage, and associated IT equipment.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: India's IT Hardware Market to See Robust Growth Driven by Digitalization
viewpoints.description: IBEF expresses a positive outlook on the Indian IT Hardware market, which includes enterprise devices. The market reached US$22.61 billion in 2026 and is projected to grow to US$31.39 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 6.78%. This growth is attributed to increasing demand for digital transformation and enterprise IT infrastructure across various sectors, signaling sustained expansion for servers, storage, enterprise PCs, and peripherals.
viewpoints.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

viewpoints.title: Data Centers and GCCs Drive Significant Demand for Enterprise Hardware Infrastructure
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that emerging growth sectors like data centers and Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are expected to significantly increase demand for resources such as water, energy, and raw materials. This implicitly signals a strong positive demand for underlying enterprise IT hardware, including servers, storage, and networking equipment, which are critical for the operations of these high-growth sectors, pushing the need for more efficient and robust devices.
viewpoints.source_title: Circular economy as growth lever for Agrasar Bharat: Reimagining water and waste economy

viewpoints.title: Advanced Analytics and Generative AI to Intensify Computing Hardware Requirements
viewpoints.description: Bain & Company posits that advanced analytics and generative AI will compound gains across B2B ecosystem players, potentially orchestrating entire trade lifecycles. This shift towards AI-driven operations necessitates substantial investments in high-performance computing hardware, including advanced servers and storage solutions, to handle the immense processing and data requirements of AI models, thereby creating a significant demand for sophisticated enterprise devices.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s Next Growth Frontier: B2B Commerce, Payments, and Credit

viewpoints.title: India's Overall IT Spending Driven by Data Center Expansion and AI Investments
viewpoints.description: IBEF forecasts India's IT spending to reach US$176.3 billion in 2026, strongly driven by data-center expansion and AI-enabled software investments. This indicates a robust demand environment for enterprise devices, as data centers require massive deployments of servers and storage, and AI applications necessitate powerful, specialized hardware. This trend solidifies the positive trajectory for Computer Hardware & Enterprise Devices.
viewpoints.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India
